snippet.title: The iPhone That Bent in Your Pocket
snippet.description:
When Apple launched the iPhone 6 in 2014, it introduced a larger display and an incredibly thin aluminum body. Not long after release, users began sharing photos of phones that had slightly bent after being carried in their pockets. The internet quickly gave the controversy a name: "Bendgate."

While later testing showed it took significant force to permanently bend the phone, the viral photos and videos turned Bendgate into one of the biggest product controversies in smartphone history.

snippet.title: China Would NEVER Copy this!
snippet.description:
China has copied smartphones, rockets, and fighter jets. But one machine has defeated every attempt — ASML's EUV Lithography Machine. It is the only device in the world that can print circuits onto advanced chips using 13.5 nanometer light — the smaller the circuit, the more powerful the chip. Every advanced chip from Nvidia, Apple, Intel, and TSMC runs through this machine. ASML is the only company that builds it. The mirrors inside come exclusively from Germany's Zeiss — and Zeiss sells to nobody else. The machine has around 1 lakh parts sourced from 5,000 companies across the world. China could copy the blueprints tomorrow and still not build it — because the real barrier is 40 years of supplier relationships, precision expertise, and institutional knowledge that does not exist anywhere else on the planet.
